# Bundled wallpapers

These JPEGs ship inside the image and are served same-origin at
`/assets/wallpapers/<file>` with a year-long immutable cache (rule three:
nothing is fetched from a third party at runtime). A canvas background of the
kind `{ "type": "wallpaper", "id": … }` names one by its catalogue id in
`apps/server/src/wallpapers.ts`; the manifest carries the file names the
server resolved, and the wall picks the smaller or the larger one by its own
pixel size.

**Generated by `scripts/wallpapers/generate.mjs`, and licensed under this
project's own licence (AGPL-3.0-or-later; see `NOTICE`).** Every wallpaper is
a parametric SVG drawn from a seed by that script and rasterised by the
bundled headless Chromium, so there is no stock-photo licence question —
stock licences often forbid redistribution in a bundle — and a wallpaper is
regenerated or changed by editing its drawing or its seed. The catalogue the
server reads, `apps/server/src/wallpaper-catalogue.ts`, is written by the same
script, with each picture's mean colour and luminance measured off the raster.

The set is the twenty-six of plan item P6.2 (Q10): soft gradients, paper and
textures, contour lines, geometric shapes, landscapes, the four seasons, and
two for fun. Fourteen are dark and twelve light; every one is held, from the
bytes it ships as, to 4.5:1 for the text of every built-in theme of its tone
through the Soft widget ground (`browser-wallpaper-contrast.test.ts`), and a
wallpaper that fails that does not ship.

The file names are content-hashed (`<id>-<long edge>.<hash>.jpg`), so an
edited picture is a new URL and a year of caching on a wall stays honest.
`wallpapers.test.ts` holds every name in the catalogue to the bytes on disk,
and the directory's total size to a 15 MB budget.
